```{r}
#| label: setup
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(classInt)

# Number of classes for each map
n_equal <- 5
n_jenks <- 5

# Equal Earth projection (equal-area, suited to choropleths)
crs_map <- "+proj=eqearth +lon_0=0"
```

## Data and boundaries

Data: *Women's Political Empowerment Index* (0 = lowest, 1 = highest), [Our World in Data, 2025](https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/women-political-empowerment-index?tab=table&time=2025).
Boundaries: Natural Earth via `rnaturalearth`.
Countries without data are shown in grey.

### About the index
**Women's political empowerment** is defined as a process of increasing capacity for women, leading to greater choice, agency, and participation in societal decision-making. It is understood to incorporate three equally-weighted dimensions: fundamental civil liberties, women's open discussion of political issues and participation in civil society organizations, and the descriptive representation of women in formal political positions.

The index is made up of three sub-indices: women's civil liberties, women's civil society participation, and women's political participation (see[https://ourworldindata.org/women-rights](Women's Rights topic page).).

```{r}
#| label: data
dat <- read_csv("Data/OurWinData2026-women-political-empowerment-index.csv",
                show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  rename(index = `Women's Political Empowerment Index`,
         region = `World region according to OWID`)

world_ll <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf") |>
  filter(adm0_a3 != "ATA") |>                       # Antarctica is not a country
  mutate(Code = case_when(
    adm0_a3 == "KOS"                ~ "OWID_KOS",    # Kosovo
    adm0_a3 %in% c("IOA", "ATC")    ~ NA_character_, # Australian external territories
    TRUE                            ~ iso_a3_eh      # fixes France / Norway
  ),
  area_m2 = as.numeric(st_area(geometry))) |>
  left_join(dat, by = "Code")

world <- st_transform(world_ll, crs_map)

# Sanity check: every country in the data set is on the map
stopifnot(all(dat$Code %in% world$Code))
cat(nrow(dat), "countries with data;",
    sum(is.na(world$index)), "map units without data (grey)\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: helpers
# Build class labels from break values; classes use the exact breaks
classify <- function(x, breaks, digits = 2) {
  lab <- paste0(formatC(head(breaks, -1), format = "f", digits = digits), " to ",
                formatC(tail(breaks, -1), format = "f", digits = digits))
  factor(cut(x, breaks, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = lab), levels = lab)
}

# Small countries are invisible at world scale: add a marker so all are represented
small <- world |>
  filter(!is.na(index), area_m2 < 2.5e10) |>   # < 25,000 km²
  st_point_on_surface()

map_theme <- theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
        panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),   # white oceans
        legend.position  = "bottom",
        legend.title     = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
        plot.caption     = element_text(colour = "grey35", hjust = 0))

make_map <- function(fills, title, subtitle, legend_title,
                     w = world, sm = small, context = NULL, window = NULL,
                     dot_size = 1.6, caption_extra = "") {
  ggplot() +
    {if (!is.null(context))
      geom_sf(data = context, fill = "grey96", colour = "white", linewidth = 0.15)} +
    geom_sf(data = w, aes(fill = cls), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.15) +
    geom_sf(data = sm, aes(fill = cls), shape = 21, size = dot_size,
            colour = "grey25", stroke = 0.25, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = fills, na.value = "grey80", drop = FALSE,
                      name = legend_title, na.translate = TRUE,
                      labels = function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "No data", x),
                      guide = guide_legend(nrow = 1, title.position = "top",
                                           override.aes = list(colour = "grey40"))) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle,
         caption = paste0("Source: Our World in Data, Women's Political Empowerment Index, 2025. Boundaries: Natural Earth.",
                          caption_extra)) +
    {if (!is.null(window))
      coord_sf(xlim = window$x, ylim = window$y, expand = FALSE)} +
    map_theme
}
```

## Map 1 — Equal intervals, single purple hue

Classes of equal width across the observed range; lightness of one hue encodes the level.

```{r}
#| label: map-equal
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-alt: "World choropleth map of the Women's Political Empowerment Index in 2025, five equal-interval classes in a light-to-dark purple scale. Countries without data are grey."
br_equal <- seq(min(dat$index), max(dat$index), length.out = n_equal + 1)
world$cls <- classify(world$index, br_equal)
small$cls <- classify(small$index, br_equal)

purples <- c("#f2f0f7", "#cbc9e2", "#9e9ac8", "#756bb1", "#54278f")

make_map(purples,
         "Women's Political Empowerment Index, 2025",
         "Equal-interval classes, sequential purple scale",
         "Index (0 to 1)")
```

## Map 2 — Jenks natural breaks, a different hue for each level

Jenks breaks minimise within-class variance, so class limits follow gaps in the data.
A diverging, colour-blind-safe palette gives each level its own hue (red → yellow → blue).

```{r}
#| label: map-jenks
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-alt: "World choropleth map of the Women's Political Empowerment Index in 2025, five Jenks natural-break classes shown in distinct hues from red (lowest) through yellow to blue (highest). Countries without data are grey."
br_jenks <- classIntervals(dat$index, n = n_jenks, style = "jenks")$brks
world$cls <- classify(world$index, br_jenks)
small$cls <- classify(small$index, br_jenks)

hues <- c("#d7191c", "#fdae61", "#ffffbf", "#abd9e9", "#2c7bb6")   # RdYlBu, 5 classes

make_map(hues,
         "Women's Political Empowerment Index, 2025",
         "Jenks natural breaks, distinct hue per level",
         "Index (0 to 1)")
```

#| label: map-jenks-Qualitative
#| fig-width: 11

#| fig-alt: "World choropleth map of the Women's Political Empowerment Index in 2025."
br_jenks <- classIntervals(dat$index, n = n_jenks, style = "jenks")$brks
world$cls <- classify(world$index, br_jenks)
small$cls <- classify(small$index, br_jenks)

Qhues <- c('#377eb8', '#984ea3', '#4daf4a',"#ffff33", "#a65628")  #  5 classes

## Asia-Pacific focus

Same two maps, zoomed to the Asia-Pacific region (UN ESCAP member States in Asia and the Pacific).
**Class breaks are the global ones** from Maps 1 and 2, so colours mean the same thing as above.
Countries outside the region are shown in light grey for context; "No data" stays darker grey.
Map 3 uses a single **green** hue; Map 4 keeps a distinct hue per level.

```{r}
#| label: ap-setup
# ESCAP regional members (geographic Asia-Pacific; excludes FRA, GBR, NLD, USA)
ap_codes <- c("AFG","ARM","AUS","AZE","BGD","BTN","BRN","KHM","CHN","FJI","GEO","IND",
              "IDN","IRN","JPN","KAZ","KIR","PRK","KOR","KGZ","LAO","MYS","MDV","MHL",
              "FSM","MNG","MMR","NRU","NPL","NZL","PAK","PLW","PNG","PHL","RUS","WSM",
              "SGP","SLB","LKA","TJK","THA","TLS","TON","TUR","TKM","TUV","UZB","VUT","VNM")

crs_ap <- "+proj=eqearth +lon_0=120"            # centred on the region; Pacific stays in one piece

# Crop to the region's longitude window (25E to 145W) on both sides of the antimeridian
suppressMessages(sf_use_s2(FALSE))
box <- function(x0, x1) st_as_sfc(st_bbox(c(xmin = x0, xmax = x1, ymin = -50, ymax = 80), crs = 4326))
world_ap <- bind_rows(suppressWarnings(st_crop(world_ll, box(25, 180))),
                      suppressWarnings(st_crop(world_ll, box(-180, -145)))) |>
  mutate(in_ap = Code %in% ap_codes) |>
  st_transform(crs_ap)
suppressMessages(sf_use_s2(TRUE))

ap_data <- world_ap |> filter(in_ap)
ap_ctx  <- world_ap |> filter(!in_ap) |> st_geometry() |> st_sf()

ap_data$cls_equal <- classify(ap_data$index, br_equal)
ap_data$cls_jenks <- classify(ap_data$index, br_jenks)

ap_small <- ap_data |> filter(area_m2 < 2.5e10) |>   # also no-data micro-states (shown grey)
  st_point_on_surface() |> suppressWarnings()

# Map window in projected coordinates
corner <- st_sfc(st_point(c(25, 0)), st_point(c(-145, 0)),
                 st_point(c(120, -48)), st_point(c(120, 78)), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(crs_ap) |> st_coordinates()
ap_window <- list(x = sort(corner[1:2, "X"]), y = sort(corner[3:4, "Y"]))

# Which ESCAP members have no index value?
missing_ap <- setdiff(ap_codes, dat$Code)
cat("ESCAP members without data (grey):", ifelse(length(missing_ap), paste(missing_ap, collapse = ", "), "none"), "\n")
```

### Map 3 — Equal intervals, single green hue

```{r}
#| label: map-ap-equal
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| fig-alt: "Asia-Pacific choropleth map of the Women's Political Empowerment Index in 2025, five equal-interval classes in a light-to-dark green scale. Countries without data are grey; countries outside the region are light grey."
greens <- c("#d9f0d3", "#a6dba0", "#5aae61", "#1b7837", "#00441b")
w3 <- ap_data |> mutate(cls = cls_equal)
s3 <- ap_small |> mutate(cls = cls_equal)

make_map(greens,
         "Women's Political Empowerment Index, 2025: Asia-Pacific",
         "Equal-interval classes (global breaks), sequential green scale",
         "Index (0 to 1)",
         w = w3, sm = s3, context = ap_ctx, window = ap_window, dot_size = 2.4,
         caption_extra = " Light grey: outside focus region.")
```

```{r}
#| label: map-ap-jenks
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| fig-alt: "Asia-Pacific choropleth map of the Women's Political Empowerment Index in 2025, five Jenks natural-break classes in distinct hues from red (lowest) through yellow to blue (highest). Countries without data are grey; countries outside the region are light grey."
w4 <- ap_data |> mutate(cls = cls_jenks)
s4 <- ap_small |> mutate(cls = cls_jenks)

```

## Proportional symbol maps

Instead of colouring countries, each country gets a symbol placed inside it whose size encodes the
index value (0 to 1). Countries are drawn light grey; countries **without data** are darker grey and carry no symbol.
Symbols sit at an interior point of each country, so overlaps are expected in crowded areas (Europe, Caribbean, Pacific).

```{r}
#| label: prop-setup
# Interior point of each country with data; draw large symbols first so small ones stay visible
pts <- world |>
  filter(!is.na(index)) |>
  st_point_on_surface() |>
  suppressWarnings()
xy  <- st_coordinates(pts)
pts <- pts |> mutate(x = xy[, "X"], y = xy[, "Y"]) |> arrange(desc(index))

sym_col <- "#54278f"   # same purple as Map 1

# Base map: light grey with data, darker grey without
prop_base <- function() {
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = world, aes(fill = is.na(index)), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.15,
            show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey92", `TRUE` = "grey78"))
}

prop_labs <- labs(title = "Women's Political Empowerment Index, 2025",
                  caption = "Source: Our World in Data, Women's Political Empowerment Index, 2025. Boundaries: Natural Earth. Dark grey: no data.")

size_scale <- scale_size_area(max_size = 8, limits = c(0, 1),
                              breaks = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1), name = "Index (0 to 1)")
size_guide <- guides(size = guide_legend(nrow = 1, title.position = "top",
                                         override.aes = list(alpha = 1)))
```

### Map 5 — Proportional circles

```{r}
#| label: map-circles
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-alt: "World map with solid purple circles at each country, circle area proportional to the Women's Political Empowerment Index in 2025. Countries without data are dark grey."
prop_base() +
  geom_point(data = pts, aes(x = x, y = y, size = index),
             shape = 21, fill = sym_col, colour = "white", stroke = 0.3) +
  size_scale + size_guide +
  prop_labs + labs(subtitle = "Proportional circles (area encodes the index)") +
  map_theme
```

### Map 6 — Proportional circles with transparency

Semi-transparent fill with a solid outline keeps overlapping circles readable.

```{r}
#| label: map-circles-alpha
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-alt: "World map with semi-transparent purple circles with dark outlines at each country, circle area proportional to the Women's Political Empowerment Index in 2025. Countries without data are dark grey."
prop_base() +
  geom_point(data = pts, aes(x = x, y = y, size = index),
             shape = 21, fill = sym_col, alpha = 0.45, colour = sym_col, stroke = 0.5) +
  size_scale + size_guide +
  prop_labs + labs(subtitle = "Proportional circles with transparency (area encodes the index)") +
  map_theme
```

### Map 7 — Proportional bars

Bar height is proportional to the index; the reference bars in the lower left show the scale.

```{r}
#| label: map-bars
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-alt: "World map with vertical purple bars standing on each country, bar height proportional to the Women's Political Empowerment Index in 2025. Reference bars for 0.25, 0.5 and 1.0 are shown at lower left. Countries without data are dark grey."
bar_h <- 2.2e6   # map units (metres) for an index of 1
bar_w <- 2.2e5

bb  <- st_bbox(world)
leg <- tibble(v = c(0.25, 0.5, 1),
              x = bb["xmin"] + 1.6e6 + c(0, 1, 2) * 1.0e6,
              y = bb["ymin"] + 1.0e6)

prop_base() +
  geom_rect(data = pts, aes(xmin = x - bar_w / 2, xmax = x + bar_w / 2,
                            ymin = y, ymax = y + index * bar_h),
            fill = sym_col, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
  # reference bars
  geom_rect(data = leg, aes(xmin = x - bar_w / 2, xmax = x + bar_w / 2,
                            ymin = y, ymax = y + v * bar_h),
            fill = sym_col, colour = NA) +
  geom_text(data = leg, aes(x = x, y = y - 2.6e5, label = v), size = 3) +
  annotate("text", x = bb["xmin"] + 1.6e6 - 1.5e5, y = bb["ymin"] + 1.0e6 + bar_h + 3.0e5,
           label = "Index (0 to 1)", hjust = 0, fontface = "bold", size = 3.6) +
  prop_labs + labs(subtitle = "Proportional bars (height encodes the index)") +
  map_theme
```

### Asia-Pacific focus: proportional symbols (green)

The same three symbol types, zoomed to the Asia-Pacific region defined above, in green.
Light grey: outside the focus region; dark grey: no data.

```{r}
#| label: prop-ap-setup
sym_green <- "#1b7837"
sym_red <- "darkred"

pts_ap <- ap_data |>
  filter(!is.na(index)) |>
  st_point_on_surface() |>
  suppressWarnings()
xy_ap  <- st_coordinates(pts_ap)
pts_ap <- pts_ap |> mutate(x = xy_ap[, "X"], y = xy_ap[, "Y"]) |> arrange(desc(index))

prop_base_ap <- function() {
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = ap_ctx, fill = "grey96", colour = "white", linewidth = 0.15) +
    geom_sf(data = ap_data, aes(fill = is.na(index)), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.15,
            show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey90", `TRUE` = "grey75")) +
    coord_sf(xlim = ap_window$x, ylim = ap_window$y, expand = FALSE)
}

prop_labs_ap <- labs(title = "Women's Political Empowerment Index, 2025: Asia-Pacific",
                     caption = "Source: Our World in Data, Women's Political Empowerment Index, 2025. Boundaries: Natural Earth.\nDark grey: no data; light grey: outside focus region.")

size_scale_ap <- scale_size_area(max_size = 11, limits = c(0, 1),
                                 breaks = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1), name = "Index (0 to 1)")
```

#### Map 10 — Proportional bars (Asia-Pacific)

```{r}
#| label: map-ap-bars
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| fig-alt: "Asia-Pacific map with vertical green bars standing on each country, bar height proportional to the Women's Political Empowerment Index in 2025. Reference bars for 0.25, 0.5 and 1.0 are shown at lower left. Countries without data are dark grey."

# Bar size:  Bars are drawn in map units, which are metres in the Equal Earth projection. A gap of 1 would be 2,200 km tall, and every bar is 260 km wide.

bar_h_ap <- 2.2e6
bar_w_ap <- 2.6e5

# Legend data: Three reference bars, with values 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75. They are spaced 1,000 km apart and positioned from the lower-left corner of ap_window, which is an empty area of the map.

leg_ap <- tibble(v = c(0.25, 0.5, 1),
                 x = ap_window$x[1] + 1.2e6 + c(0, 1, 2) * 1.0e6,
                 y = ap_window$y[1] + 0.9e6)

# pts_ap is built in the setup chunk by keeping each country’s largest polygon and taking a point inside it. Without that step, countries such as Malaysia, the Philippines and Japan could have their bars placed on a distant island.

prop_base_ap() +
  geom_rect(data = pts_ap, aes(xmin = x - bar_w_ap / 2, xmax = x + bar_w_ap / 2,
                               ymin = y, ymax = y + index * bar_h_ap),
            fill = sym_green, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
  geom_rect(data = leg_ap, aes(xmin = x - bar_w_ap / 2, xmax = x + bar_w_ap / 2,
                               ymin = y, ymax = y + v * bar_h_ap),
            fill = sym_green, colour = NA) +
  geom_text(data = leg_ap, aes(x = x, y = y - 2.6e5, label = v), size = 3) +
  annotate("text",
           x = ap_window$x[1] + 1.2e6 - 1.5e5,
           y = ap_window$y[1] + 0.9e6 + bar_h_ap + 3.0e5,
           label = "Index (0 to 1)",
           hjust = 0, fontface = "bold", size = 3.6) +
  prop_labs_ap +
  labs(subtitle = "Proportional bars (height encodes the index)") +
  map_theme
```

#### Map 11 — Proportional bars with reverse index (Asia-Pacific)

Reversing the index for a better representation of **low** values.

>Low empowermentis now large bars.  


```{r}
#| label: map-ap-bars-gap
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| fig-alt: "Asia-Pacific map with vertical green bars standing on each country, bar height proportional to 1 minus the Women's Political Empowerment Index in 2025, so taller bars mean a larger gap to full empowerment. A dark dot marks the base of each bar. Reference bars for 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75 are shown at lower left. Countries without data are dark grey."

#
pts_ap_gap <- pts_ap |>
  mutate(gap = 1 - index) |>
  arrange(desc(gap))                                      # draw tall bars first

# Bars height
bar_h_ap <- 2.2e6   # map units (metres) for a gap of 1
bar_w_ap <- 2.6e5   

leg_ap <- tibble(v = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75),
                 x = ap_window$x[1] + 1.2e6 + c(0, 1, 2) * 1.0e6,
                 y = ap_window$y[1] + 0.9e6)

prop_base_ap() +
  geom_rect(data = pts_ap_gap, aes(xmin = x - bar_w_ap / 2, xmax = x + bar_w_ap / 2,
                                   ymin = y, ymax = y + gap * bar_h_ap),
            fill = sym_red, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
  # dot marking the anchor point where each bar stands
  geom_point(data = pts_ap_gap, aes(x = x, y = y), size = 0.8, colour = "darkred") +
  
  # reference bars
  geom_rect(data = leg_ap, aes(xmin = x - bar_w_ap / 2, xmax = x + bar_w_ap / 2,
                               ymin = y, ymax = y + v * bar_h_ap),
            fill = sym_red, colour = NA) +
  geom_text(data = leg_ap, aes(x = x, y = y - 2.6e5, label = v), size = 3) +
  annotate("text", x = ap_window$x[1] + 1.2e6 - 1.5e5, y = ap_window$y[1] + 0.9e6 + bar_h_ap + 3.0e5,
           label = "1 - index", hjust = 0, fontface = "bold", size = 3.6) +
  prop_labs_ap + labs(subtitle = "Proportional bars: gap to full empowerment (1 - index); taller = less empowerment") +
  map_theme
```




## Ranking of all countries

Horizontal bars, ordered from highest to lowest index. The dashed line marks the **0.5 (50%) threshold**.
Asia-Pacific countries (ESCAP members, as defined above) are in green; all other countries are in light purple.

```{r}
#| label: ranking
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 32
#| fig-alt: "Horizontal bar chart ranking 175 countries by Women's Political Empowerment Index in 2025, highest at top. A dashed vertical line marks the 0.5 threshold. Asia-Pacific countries are green, all others light purple."
rank_df <- dat |>
  mutate(group = ifelse(Code %in% ap_codes, "Asia-Pacific (ESCAP members)", "Other countries"))

n_below  <- sum(rank_df$index < 0.5)
n_ap_below <- sum(rank_df$index < 0.5 & rank_df$group != "Other countries")

ggplot(rank_df, aes(x = index, y = reorder(Entity, index), fill = group)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", index)), hjust = -0.2, size = 2.2, colour = "grey25") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8, colour = "darkred") +
  annotate("label", x = 0.5, y = 3, label = "0.5 threshold", size = 3, fill = "white",
           label.size = 0, hjust = -0.1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Asia-Pacific (ESCAP members)" = "#1b7837",
                               "Other countries"              = "#cbc9e2"),
                    name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.05), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(title = "Women's Political Empowerment Index, 2025",
       subtitle = paste0(n_below, " of ", nrow(rank_df), " countries score below 0.5 (",
                         n_ap_below, " in Asia-Pacific)"),
       x = "Index (0 to 1)", y = NULL,
       caption = "Source: Our World in Data, Women's Political Empowerment Index, 2025.") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6.5),
        legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left",
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        plot.caption = element_text(colour = "grey35", hjust = 0),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA))
```


## Ranking in Asia- Pacific

We also changed the ordering of the bar **from lowest to highest** index. The dashed line marks the **0.5 (50%) threshold**. Asia-Pacific countries only. 

```{r}
#| label: ranking-AP
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 32
#| fig-alt: "Horizontal bar chart ranking 175 countries by Women's Political Empowerment Index in 2025, highest at top. A dashed vertical line marks the 0.5 threshold. Asia-Pacific countries are green, all others light purple."

rank_df_AP <- dat %>%
  filter(Code %in% ap_codes) 
  # mutate(group = ifelse(Code %in% ap_codes, "Asia-Pacific (ESCAP members)", "Other countries"))
  # n_below  <- sum(rank_df$index < 0.5)
  # n_ap_below <- sum(rank_df$index < 0.5 & rank_df$group != "Other countries")
  

rank_df_AP %>%
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = index, y = reorder(Entity, -index)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8, fill = "#1b7837") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", index)), hjust = -0.2, size = 3.2, colour = "grey25") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8, colour = "darkred") +
  annotate("label", x = 0.5, y = 3, label = "0.5 threshold", size = 3, fill = "white",
           label.size = 0, hjust = -0.1) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.05), 
                     breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(title = "Women's Political Empowerment Index, 2025",
       subtitle = paste0(n_ap_below, " of ", nrow(rank_df_AP),"
                         countries in Asia-Pacific score below 0.5"),
       x = "Index (0 to 1)",
       y = NULL,
       caption = "Source: Our World in Data, Women's Political Empowerment Index, 2025.") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8.5),
        legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left",
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        plot.caption = element_text(colour = "grey35", hjust = 0),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA))
```
